findings.issue: と is analyzed as conditional/temporal, but it is the quotative と marking the content of 祈る (pray/hope THAT). The record's own en ('Let's hope times change') reflects the quotative reading; 'when times change, let's pray' is a wrong grammar fact.
findings.current: Uses と in a conditional/temporal sense ('when/if it changes'): 時代が変わると = 'when the times change'.
findings.suggested: と is quotative, marking the content of 祈ろう: 'let's pray/hope that the times change' — 時代が変わる is what is hoped for, not a when/if clause.

findings.issue: Same wrong grammar fact as expl_en: と here is the quotative particle (content of the prayer/hope), not conditional/temporal 'quando/se'.
findings.current: A frase usa a partícula と num sentido condicional/temporal ('quando/se mudar'): 時代が変わると = 'quando os tempos mudarem'.
findings.suggested: と é citativo: marca o conteúdo de 祈ろう — 'vamos rezar/torcer para que os tempos mudem'; 時代が変わる é o que se deseja, não uma condição.

findings.issue: Literal renders と as a temporal clause; the structure is [content]と + 祈ろう (quotative), so the literal meaning is 'let us pray that the times change', matching the natural en. Current version is a sense-changing misparse.
findings.current: When the times change, let us pray.
findings.suggested: Let us pray that the times change.

findings.issue: Same misparse as lit_en: と tratado como 'quando'; the literal must mirror the quoted content clause of 祈る, not a temporal clause.
findings.current: Os tempos quando mudarem, vamos rezar/torcer.

findings.issue: 変わる heads the quoted content clause of 祈る, not a conditional clause. The token note ('seguida da partícula と (condicional/quando)' / 'particle と (conditional/when)') repeats the same error and needs the same fix.
findings.suggested: verbo da oração citada (conteúdo do desejo/da oração)

findings.issue: いくら asks about an amount/price ('how much'); 'how many' (a count) would be いくつ. The pt ('Quanto você quer?') and the いくら token gloss ('how much (quantity/price)') already say 'how much', so en is the odd one out.

ほしい means 'wanted/desired', not 'dear/priced'; as written the literal turns the sentence into a price question ('how much does it cost' = いくらですか), a different sense. The expl itself correctly says ほしい is lit. 'desired/coveted'.

Misleading claim: the particle-less form is standard at every register — いくらがほしい is unnatural even in polite speech (いくらほしいですか), so the absence of が is not an informal omission. It also clashes with the expl's own statement that いくら is an adverb.
findings.current: The particle が that would mark the desired object in 〜がほしい is omitted (informal)
findings.suggested: いくら attaches adverbially with no particle at any register (polite: いくらほしいですか); 〜がほしい would mark the implicit object (e.g. お金が), not いくら.

findings.issue: Same wrong claim as expl_en: attributes the absence of が to informality, but いくらがほしい is unnatural in any register; polite いくらほしいですか also has no particle.
findings.current: A partícula が, que normalmente marcaria o objeto desejado no padrão 〜がほしい (o alvo alvo), foi omitida por ser fala informal
findings.suggested: いくら liga-se adverbialmente sem partícula em qualquer registro (polido: いくらほしいですか); 〜がほしい marcaria o objeto implícito (ex.: お金が), não いくら.

findings.issue: どうも is a single adverb, but the dissection splits it into どう + も, teaching that どう alone means 'thanks' and presenting も as if it were the particle も (null-glossed like real particles). The token walk should treat どうも as one unit with the thanks gloss/role.
findings.suggested: (merge どう+も into one token どうも glossed 'thanks'; も here is not the particle も)
